profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer — Retired
profile.summary:
I’m in the middle of a big identity shift: transitioning from Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft to full‑time retiree. After 18 years building and maintaining systems and features across Download Center, Microsoft Homepage, Universal Store, Dynamics 365 eCommerce, Power Pages, and Power Platform, I’m stepping away from production deadlines and into a slower, more self-directed rhythm.

My career has had a few chapters — SDET, DevOps, full‑stack engineer — and a few past lives before Microsoft, including web developer, contractor, and (yes) zookeeper. It turns out that calmly handling unpredictable creatures translates surprisingly well to software.

As I wrap up my time at Microsoft, I’m focusing on personal coding projects, local exploration, and writing about the transition into early retirement. My employment history is fully updated here, partly for authenticity and partly because it’s nice to see the whole arc in one place.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
After Azure CMS was retired, I shifted into Power Pages and later Power Apps, taking on telemetry ownership and eventually UX work across Power Platform Core. This era included both reinvention and closure — the final chapter of my Microsoft career.

Highlights:
Built front‑end features for Power Pages using React and Typescript
Took ownership of Power Apps telemetry, modernizing ingestion pipelines and ensuring compliance
Shut down under‑utilized infrastructure and improved reliability
Earned my final promotion through leadership in telemetry
After a reorg, contributed UX updates to Power Platform Core (Forms Designer, View Designer)
Leveraged AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate development
Ultimately chose to retire under VRP after 18 years, closing my career on my own terms

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Promoted to Senior based on my work designing a lightweight job system and owning complex localization and integration flows. This era included commercializing internal systems, building large‑scale import/export features, and supporting multiple CMS platforms simultaneously.

Highlights:
Helped build Site Builder, the commercial successor to RedTiger for Dynamics 365 eCommerce
Designed and implemented the job system that earned my promotion to Senior
Built omni‑channel integration and bulk operations capable of processing tens of thousands of images
Maintained and extended Azure CMS, the backend powering RedTiger, MSN, and internal systems
Continued to support legacy systems (RedTiger, SiteMuse) during the transition
Participated in major COGS reduction efforts prior to Azure CMS shutdown

positions.title: Software Engineer 2 (SDET II → Dev)
positions.description:
This was the era where I transitioned from test to development — a lateral move that became the turning point of my career. I worked on SiteMuse, then moved into backend development, service design, and eventually the systems that shaped my professional identity.

Highlights:
Continued work on SiteMuse, the CMS powering the Microsoft Homepage
Transitioned from SDET II → Software Engineer, taking on my first dev project (Dante → DashContent)
Learned to build and maintain RESTful .NET services
Worked on CDS (Commerce Data Services) and partnered with RedTiger, integrating CMS and commerce systems
Owned localization pipelines (JSON ↔ XLIFF), import/export automation, and multi‑platform XLIFF support
Designed systems that only a handful of engineers fully understood
Mentored by senior engineers who helped shape my engineering craft (dependency injection, interfaces, clean architecture)

positions.title: Software Development Engineer in Test
positions.description:
I worked across several generations of Microsoft’s internal content systems, supporting properties like Download Center and the Microsoft Homepage. This era covered everything from ingestion pipelines to homepage rendering, and from manual deployments to early automation.

Highlights:
Supported Download Center, Homepage CMS (InfoPath), and early attempts to unify Microsoft’s download platforms
Built and maintained UI automation for web clients (Coded UI, Selenium)
Coordinated manual deployments, including late‑night homepage pushes
Helped onboard teams to early Git adoption (including the infamous Git server under a desk)
Worked across multiple orgs during reorg-heavy years, adapting to new systems and expectations

positions.title: Software Engineer in Test
positions.description:
Supported the CMS powering the Microsoft.com homepage — one of the most visible surfaces at the company.

Served as an SDET, my first role outside pure web development.

Wrote test plans, designed test cases, and participated in deployments.

Gained first experience with serialization/deserialization.

Completed a full contract term, took the mandatory break, and returned for a second term.

Halfway through that second term, I was converted to FTE — a milestone worth a steak dinner.

positions.title: Sharepoint Consultant
positions.description:
In‑house role at RedTech focused on client web projects and SharePoint integration.

Worked on multiple client sites across the region.

Spent significant time on SharePoint adoption and customization (it never clicked).

Learned that consulting was not a good fit for your working style.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Short contract supporting the Visual Studio team.

Built a backend ingestion system for third‑party help content.

Documented the pipeline and supported extension authors.

First exposure to developer‑ecosystem tooling.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Left a full‑time job for a one‑year contract at Xbox — one of the most pivotal decisions of my career.

Got the job because I was a gamer who could talk intelligently about upcoming titles (including Project Ego, later Fable).

Worked on Xbox.com (then written in VB.NET).

Helped build internal authoring tools and learned about content caching at scale.

Integrated Microsoft Passport into Xbox.com, enabling early Xbox Live identity.

Helped test Xbox Live before launch.

First of many CMS systems I'd work with.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Worked on web‑based tracking for intermodal shipping containers (ships, trains, trucks).

Hired partly because I took notes on a Pocket PC, which aligned with their vision for mobile container tracking.

Built a SOAP client for the Pocket PC.

Wrote COM objects in VB.NET — my first real automation work.

Traveled to Washington, D.C. for training on industry data‑format conversion systems.

Called customers when their morning data feeds didn’t arrive (I hated phone calls then too).

Learned that long commutes + dress codes + consulting‑style expectations = not my ideal environment.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Recruited during the DotCom boom for a Microsoft contract — flown from Milwaukee to Seattle and back in a single day for a temp interview.

Hired on the spot for the SiteBuilder Network (later merged into MSDN).

Worked on internal tooling and developer‑facing systems.

After MPL2 merged with Saltmine, contributed to large client projects.

Joined a top‑secret BP rebrand project in downtown Seattle; delivered on time with zero leaks.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
Worked on time‑and‑attendance solutions for healthcare organizations.

Customized Internet Explorer branding, including animating a custom browser throbber.

Created graphics and animated GIFs despite having no formal design training.

Learned classic ASP, ADO, and early database‑driven web development.

Built web interfaces that mimicked native Windows apps — a novelty at the time.

positions.title: Wizard / Webmaster
positions.description:
Promoted into the university’s wonderfully earnest “Wizard Program”, serving as the campus Web Master during the earliest days of the web.

Held keys to the server room and the library’s front door (just the lobby, but still).

Performed regular DAT backups of the university website.

Built UWSP’s first site map, onboarded departments and clubs, and taught workshops on HTML.

Wrote the university’s first web publishing manual.
Enforced early web policy, including revoking the rugby team’s site for linking to porn.

positions.title: Student Computer Lab Assistant
positions.description:
Supported multiple campus computer labs during the early PC era. Trusted with keys to the labs, responsible for opening/closing shifts, and keeping everything running smoothly.

Manually booted 8086 PCs from 5.25" floppies (one at a time, because automation was still a rumor).

Became adept at unjamming dot‑matrix printers using whatever tools were available.

Diagnosed issues in daisy‑chained networks, tracking down the one machine taking down the whole row.

Helped panicked students before deadlines, learning early lessons in calm triage and quiet leadership.

positions.title: Software Cataloger / Web Dev
positions.description:
Shareware Cataloger (Part‑Time)

Started as a customer of a Marshfield BBS that later evolved into a full ISP — then became a part‑time employee

Categorized incoming shareware titles by reading descriptions and assigning tags — a surprisingly manual process that felt “library adjacent,” even if the ingestion pipeline was… let’s say primitive.

Web Developer (Promoted)

Built early websites for local businesses, including a Wisconsin ginseng farm and a Jackson Hole ski resort, during the era when “web developer” meant hand‑coding everything.

Was asked to produce both a website and a Gopher portal from the same source files — a request that was, even then, hilariously unworkable.

Worked primarily from home, long before remote work was mainstream.

Occasionally commuted to Marshfield, but most of the job was early‑era WFH — decades before COVID made it normal.

positions.title: Zookeeper
positions.description:
Served as a zookeeper intern, assisting with daily care across the entire collection and gaining hands‑on experience with a wide range of species.

Hand‑fed ring‑tailed lemurs bits of banana and learned to avoid being run over by an overly enthusiastic young zebu.

Became a launch platform for baby goats, discovering just how tiny pygmy goat kids really are.

Bottle‑fed twin deer fawns, learning the surprisingly tricky art of mixing powdered formula correctly.

Took bear cubs on supervised walks; they attacked my ankles in protest when I wouldn’t let them play with cigarette butts on the ground.

Practiced kindness with visitors by letting families with small children pick out the peacock train feathers first, even though I wanted one too.

Learned to operate both a push‑behind lawn mower and a John Deere utility tractor, contributing to grounds maintenance.

Found a quiet joy in hosing down the pathways before the zoo opened — a moment of calm before the day’s chaos.

positions.title: Animal Rehabilitator
positions.description:
Provided hands‑on care for a wide range of wildlife, including songbirds, pigeons, opossums, owls, and ducks, gaining deep experience in animal handling, feeding, and rehabilitation.

Learned to work confidently with mealworms and waxworms, overcoming squeamishness through necessity and repetition.

Assisted with medical procedures, including holding a baby pigeon during stitches — and learned the importance of handing off work before you pass out under a hot operating lamp.

Participated in field rescues, including retrieving broods of ducklings from storm sewers, often in less‑than‑ideal conditions.

Accepted the catch loop to secure a raccoon with distemper, discovering a very early version of “YOLO” long before the term existed.

Developed a lifelong affection for cedar waxwings and baby crows, sparked by the intimacy of daily care.

positions.title: Crew Member
positions.description:
Learned humility early by working in fast food — an experience that permanently shaped my respect for people in service roles.

Prepared large‑batch ingredients, including cooking 20 pounds of ground beef at a time, and discovered that power tools sometimes play a surprising role in food prep.

Gained firsthand experience with high‑volume, fast‑paced teamwork and customer service during peak hours.

volunteerExperiences.description:
Volunteer Educator in multiple animal areas, including:

Small Mammals

Big Cats

Pachyderms

Key responsibilities & experiences:

Interpreted animal behavior and biology for the public, helping visitors understand species ranging from tamarins to tigers to elephants.

Assisted with crowd control for the Raptor Show, including safely escorting Rodney, a notoriously nippy Amazon parrot, back to his trailer after performances.

Supported animal moves and behind‑the‑scenes operations, including providing security during the transfer of two White Rhinos into the pachyderm building — and was rewarded with the chance to hold a rhino horn.

Participated in special events, including playing Hansel during the zoo’s Halloween program (despite being a girl, which I took in stride).

experience.title: Animal Rehabilitator
experience.description:
Provided hands‑on care for a wide range of wildlife, including songbirds, pigeons, opossums, owls, and ducks, gaining deep experience in animal handling, feeding, and rehabilitation.

Learned to work confidently with mealworms and waxworms, overcoming squeamishness through necessity and repetition.

Assisted with medical procedures, including holding a baby pigeon during stitches — and learned the importance of handing off work before you pass out under a hot operating lamp.

Participated in field rescues, including retrieving broods of ducklings from storm sewers, often in less‑than‑ideal conditions.

Accepted the catch loop to secure a raccoon with distemper, discovering a very early version of “YOLO” long before the term existed.

Developed a lifelong affection for cedar waxwings and baby crows, sparked by the intimacy of daily care.

experience.title: Crew Member
experience.description:
Learned humility early by working in fast food — an experience that permanently shaped my respect for people in service roles.

Prepared large‑batch ingredients, including cooking 20 pounds of ground beef at a time, and discovered that power tools sometimes play a surprising role in food prep.

Gained firsthand experience with high‑volume, fast‑paced teamwork and customer service during peak hours.

volunteerExperience.description:
Volunteer Educator in multiple animal areas, including:

Small Mammals

Big Cats

Pachyderms

Key responsibilities & experiences:

Interpreted animal behavior and biology for the public, helping visitors understand species ranging from tamarins to tigers to elephants.

Assisted with crowd control for the Raptor Show, including safely escorting Rodney, a notoriously nippy Amazon parrot, back to his trailer after performances.

Supported animal moves and behind‑the‑scenes operations, including providing security during the transfer of two White Rhinos into the pachyderm building — and was rewarded with the chance to hold a rhino horn.

Participated in special events, including playing Hansel during the zoo’s Halloween program (despite being a girl, which I took in stride).
